title: Inference Demand Cartography POC - Galileo Retail
summary: Initial POC scoping for cartography of inference demand: map QPS bursts, concurrency, and token length distribution to benchmark plan. Goal is to define success criteria (latency SLOs, cost targets), agree on replay data, and schedule a 2-week pilot benchmarks run against Dedicated and Hosted profiles.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~57m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Lena Morales (Redwood AE), Owen Park (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM); Priya Nair (Galileo Head of AI), Tomás Ruiz (Galileo Platform Eng), Evelyn Cho (Galileo CTO), Alex Bae (Galileo SRE)

[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro — i'm lena, i'm the ae on this. owen and marcus from our side. um, objective today is to sketch the demand cartography for your inference workloads and land on a POC test plan.
[00:20] Priya: thanks lena, yeah we've got, uh, a few things to validate — mainly burst handling and tail latency for our conversational product, plus cost per 1M tokens estimates.
[00:27] Owen: great. before we dive, can you confirm traffic shape? priya, you sent a sample trace last week but it was annotated. what are the typical qps and burst factors?
[00:40] Tomás: sure — baseline daytime qps is about 120 qps, moving to a 4x burst during promos so peaks ~480 qps for 6-12 minute windows. we also see microbursts — short sharp spikes of 800-1k qps for 30-90s when checkout flows flush.
[01:05] Lena: ok microbursts — good to know. what's the concurrency per request? are calls long-polling or quick request/response?
[01:15] Alex: mostly short requests; typical concurrency per instance is 30-60 outstanding requests during peak. average conversation length 18 turns, mean input tokens ~60, mean output ~120 but distribution is fat — there's a heavy tail when recommendations include product descriptions, can go up to 800 tokens output.
[01:43] Owen: that token tail matters for KV cache and batching. long outputs change GPU memory patterns and latency. do you have percentiles for token lengths?
[01:52] Priya: yeah we have histograms. 50th input 55, 95th 210, 99th 520. outputs: 50th 110, 95th 420, 99th 760. we can share the CSV.
[02:05] Lena: perfect. next — what latency SLOs are you targeting? 95th, 99th?
[02:12] Evelyn: for customer-facing recommendations we'd like 95th < 250ms and 99th < 600ms. backend async features can be looser. cost target: under $X per 1M tokens — i'll send procurement bucket later.
[02:30] Owen: noted. those are tight for large outputs — we should define which endpoints need strict SLOs vs best-effort. for the pilot we'll gate on the recommendation endpoint.
[02:42] Tomás: also we need to test both hosted and our private option (VPC). security is a hard req — KMS integration, audit logs, SSO.
[02:54] Marcus: yes — we can run the pilot in your VPC (private) and also run parallel hosted runs to compare economics. small note: our private package requires a light agent install — owen can outline infra later.
[03:10] Lena: ok plan outline i propose: 1) collect replay dataset (we'll take a 48h representative trace) 2) synthesize burst patterns — add promo spikes 3) run replay on dedicated baseline config and hosted config 4) capture quantiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput, GPU util, cost per token 5) analyze and recommend config (batching, quantization, instance sizing). does that align?
[03:35] Priya: yes. timeline? we need results before quarterly planning — so 3 week window?
[03:41] Lena: plausible. we typically do 2-week pilot but given your validation gates we can do 3 weeks: week 1 data prep and infra, week 2 run benchmarks, week 3 analyze and iterate.
[03:55] Owen: technical notes on benchmark: we recommend two modes — replay (exact request timing and token mix) and stress mode (sustained qps to find throughput ceiling). we'll measure tail latency under realistic KV cache hit rates and with/without prefix caching. also run quantized model variants to show cost vs latency tradeoff.
[04:20] Tomás: how do you handle model fallbacks? in prod we need predictable graceful degradation.
[04:26] Owen: we have routing polices — fallback to smaller quantized model with same API shape. for the POC we'll test main model and a 4-bit quantized variant. keep in mind output quality can degrade on long outputs, so we'll include an eval set.
[04:43] Priya: can you measure quality delta? we need to see Rouge/BLEU or human-sampled ratings for critical flows.
[04:49] Owen: yes — we'll run automated metrics and sample 200 examples for human review.
[04:55] Lena: about security: you mentioned KMS and audit logs. we have SOC2 + dedicated private package with KMS hooks. we'll share the security pack.
[05:05] Evelyn: also SAML SSO for RBAC. we must show audit trail for compliance.
[05:11] Marcus: noted — will attach SOC2 cert, network architecture, and our onboarding checklist.
[05:18] Tomás: what's the expected infra footprint for the dedicated test? we have limited GPU quota in our cloud account.
[05:25] Owen: for a 480 qps sustained with 120 token avg out, rough thumb is X A100-equivalents; but with batching and caching you can reduce. we'll dimension three candidate configs: conservative (more instances, lower util), balanced, and aggressive (higher util). we'll also include a small matrix of model quantization levels.
[05:47] Alex: can you give a rough number? we need to request cloud quota.
[05:50] Owen: rough napkin: to hit 480qps p95 < 250ms on full-precision model maybe 12 A100 v4 equivalents; 4-bit quant might cut to 5-6 equivalents. we'll refine after we run microbenchmarks on your payload.
[06:08] Priya: sounds good. we will need concrete cost estimates for each config.
[06:12] Lena: yes — part of deliverables: cost per 1M tokens and monthly burn for productionized capacity.
[06:18] Tomás: data handling — we'll sanitize traces before sharing. names and pii removed. is that ok for replay?
[06:22] Owen: absolutely. we prefer tokenized payloads but raw texts with markings work. also include flags for cacheable prefixes.
[06:34] Priya: question on observability — can we get token-level cost and per-route dashboards?
[06:39] Marcus: our console provides token-level breakdown, per-route latency, and traces. we'll share demo access during the pilot.
[06:48] Evelyn: ok next — acceptance criteria. propose: 1) p95 below 250ms and p99 below 600ms for recommendation endpoint under promo spike profile (4x baseline) 2) production cost per 1M tokens within X% of target 3) no security compliance gaps for KMS/SSO/audit logs.
[07:15] Lena: that's a good start. we'll add a quality gate: automated eval quality delta < 5% on human-rated set between baseline and quantized model.
[07:28] Tomás: how will you replay microbursts? we need sub-minute accuracy.
[07:32] Owen: our replay tool preserves inter-arrival times and temporality; we'll feed the trace and overlay synthetic microburst events. we'll run multiple seeds to account for variance.
[07:44] Alex: do you need VPN access for private runs?
[07:47] Marcus: for VPC-based private trials we request a peered subnet and a small config for the agent. won’t need full VPN — more like peering and a short-lived cert.
[07:57] Priya: ok. can you outline the exact artifacts you'll need from us?
[08:01] Lena: yes — short list: 1) 48h sanitized request trace (timestamps, request payload size, tokenized lengths preferred) 2) a list of endpoints and SLO per endpoint 3) billing target for cost gating 4) a small eval set for human review (~200 samples).
[08:18] Tomás: timeline to get started: we can produce sanitized trace by next thursday.
[08:22] Lena: great. we will draft the POC plan doc and share by monday.
[08:26] Owen: one more technical — gpu memory: long outputs can fill kv cache; we'll instrument for kv cache hit/miss and measure how cache warming affects tail latency.
[08:36] Tomás: good point. also we have some multi-turn contexts with reused prefixes; measuring prefix cache hit rate is important.
[08:43] Owen: yep we'll include prefix caching toggles in the runs.
[08:47] Priya: any other blockers?
[08:50] Evelyn: procurement — we may need an NDA or trial contract addendum to spin up dedicated runs. procurement lead is copied on follow-ups.
[08:59] Marcus: we'll send standard trial contract and scoping SOW.
[09:05] Lena: ok recap: we agreed on data artifact list, 3-week pilot timeline, two modes of benchmark (replay + stress), configs (hosted vs private vs quantized), success criteria (p95/p99, cost, quality), and deliverables (benchmarks, cost report, security docs).
[09:30] Priya: that works. next steps?
[09:33] Lena: action items and dates — i'll put in notes.

Summary notes (auto): POC will validate latency and cost under promo bursts and microbursts. Emphasis on 99th percentile token-length handling. Pilot will run in customer's VPC with parallel hosted tests. Evaluations include automated metrics + human sample.
